messages.subject: sample test data
parts:
Hi All,

I have started exploring GGIR recently for sleep detection. I have used the function create_test_acc_csv(sf = 3, Nmin = 24*60*3) to generate three night's worth of sample data; however, I found the sample accelerations not realistic. For example, the accelerations and accompanying arm movements generated are very different to what is shown in the "accelerometer data processing with GGIR" vignette, section 4 figure.

Does anyone have some sample/simulated actigraph .csv data that would clearly show sleep/wake activity to help understand and test the outputs of GGIR?

Many thanks,

Phil

----
Philippe C. Dixon, PhD, CSCS

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] sample test data
parts:
Hi Phil,

The function 'create_test_acc_csv' is not intended to mimic a real recording in such detail. It's main function is to help testing the consistency of the R package between releases, as an efficient alternative to uploading half a GB of real data (the file is created in the cloud and does not have to be uploaded).

If you cannot collect your own test data, then here is a 100Hz multi-day example file (in my own OneDrive, so i will not keep it there forever). Further, there is one example file on the Axivity webpage: https://axivity.com/downloads/ax3.
​
 001_39434_0000000003_23-02-2018.zip
​
Thanks, Vincent
